purpose: Check the three marked open-snap pairs for unique mating, square feet, hook capture and a reversible entry path, and measure the faces in the submitted Mark1 toolpaths.

wrong_pair_checks.measured_quantity: Sum of transverse widths where the cover keys and runners would occupy fixed receiver material. Values are mm. A positive value blocks the pose. Each diagonal pair accepts its centered blades with 0.62 mm side clearance.
wrong_pair_checks.axial_registration: The projected working profile equals both exported end profiles through the wings, keys and guides. Each keyed feature runs the entire 12 mm. Translating the cover along the open ends preserves the same obstruction for any positive length of axial overlap in parallel or end-for-end assembly.
wrong_pair_checks.lateral_check: Intersect the two exported working profiles on a horizontal line at receiver h27.65 and cover h19.65, with both cover orientations. Between coordinate coincidences of the interval ends, the total intersected width is linear in transverse translation. Evaluate those coincidences plus the two ends of the allowed interval.
wrong_pair_checks.roll_check: At receiver h26.60 the 0 to 5 mm closing range and ±10° of rocking about the regulator axis puts the cut across the straight portion of all four rigid blades and runners. The actual span of cover heights is 19.53 to 28.68 mm. Each transverse interval becomes its original X interval scaled by 1/cos(angle) plus a common shift. The intersections of all interval-edge equations partition scale and shift into cells where total overlap is affine. Check every cell vertex for scale 1 through 1/cos(10°) and common shift ±9 mm, covering lateral center travel ±8 mm. Repeat after end-for-end reversal.

oblique_open_end_catch.method: Boolean intersection of the two hashed free STL meshes in the registered end view. An independent repeat used the same pose and a 2 mm straight pull. The receiver stays fixed.
oblique_open_end_catch.frame: x = X − 76.5, y = Y − 439.875, h = 355 − Z, in mm. Subtract 0.10 mm more from cover h to register the nominal square seat before applying this transform.
oblique_open_end_catch.interpretation: In this fore-aft tipped pose a mismatched cover can catch the exposed ends of both shoulders under a straight pull. It slides free toward the open end. The keys prevent square seating on the wrong receiver.

methods.model: Recover both leaves from the print STL, undo the free cross-section rotation at each height, and bend about each leaf neutral axis under a load at its retaining lip. The saddle, guides and keys stay rigid. The two modeled wings each move 0.80 mm from free to square. The unloaded free crest is 2.0348° to the receiver roof, with its outer edge closer to the roof.
methods.stroke: Search 271 straight insertion positions on each side for the required outward spring displacement. For an independent continuous path start square at 0.80 mm outward spread per wing and open 1.0625 mm while increasing spread to 4.20 mm at 24 beam poses. Linearly interpolate each contour station between poses. Hold the resulting shape to 25 mm open, then release. Bound each swept edge with the convex hull of its two endpoints at either pose and check the enclosed wing areas. Reverse the same path to insert. The rigid saddle and guide path is swept separately. Working contours have a station at least every 0.10 mm. The small seated intersections are STL rounding at intended contact.
methods.deposition: Expand each native outer-wall segment by its commanded radius. Across both feet on 46 interior courses, recover the free slope and invert the cross-section rotation and neutral-axis displacement to the square pose. Read the bearing width 0.03 mm inside the face, and its height at nine points at least 0.35 mm from each modeled corner. At three axial stations register each flat face to the emitted roof, then measure both 45° shoulders at ordinary course midheight at least 0.40 mm inside the target flank. Positive shoulder projection means the profiles overlap radially if held in this straight registration. Sample the emitted crown and saddle across ±4 mm on a 0.01 mm grid. Negative crown gap indicates projected overlap.
methods.scope: The material envelope uses the commanded bead radii. Layer shape under load, actual contact pressure, hand rocking, insertion force and release force require the prints.
